newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says optimistic on rebel talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says optimistic on rebel talks.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori said on Friday contact had been resumed between his government and Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages and this was a "good sign" which raised hopes of a peaceful end to the crisis.
"We have established a bridge via today's radio contact" between government negotiator Domingo Palermo and rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, Fujimori told local radio.
Fujimori said the two men had had a cordial, four-minute conversation that had opened up "hopeful prospects".

In the conversation, Cerpa agreed to a requewst by Palermo that Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani return this weekend to the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, where the hostages have been held for more than three weeks, to celebrate Mass with the hostages.
Fujimori did not say when Palermo might return to the residence.
Palermo met Cerpa once face to face on Dec. 28 and won the release of 20 hostages.
